---
title: "Week 5 · Central Limit Theorem. t-distribution. Confidence intervals"
subtitle: "Hypothesis testing II: from the population distribution to the sampling distribution of the mean, and the t-test in practice"
---

Week 4 used t-tests; Week 5 explains where they come from. Starting from a
normally distributed population, the deck derives the sampling distribution of
the mean, the Central Limit Theorem and the standard error, introduces the
t-distribution and confidence intervals, and then practises one-sample and
two-sample t-tests on three examples. A self-study section and a set of
t-score tables close the deck.

## What the deck covers

-   **t-test with conditional cash transfers**, the example carried over from
    Week 4.
-   **Normally distributed population and confidence intervals**: the
    population distribution, the 95% interval for the mean, and 90%, 95% and
    99% intervals; the population can have any distribution.
-   **The Central Limit Theorem**, the standard error, a summary and the CLT in
    practice.
-   **The confidence interval and the t-distribution**: how to find a CI, the
    t-distribution and how it differs from the normal, from the population to a
    sample, the t-distribution in use on the travel-time example, interpreting
    and calculating a confidence interval, and more on the t-distribution and
    the t-test.
-   **Practice**: Example 1, the effect of a drug on sleep (one-sample t-test:
    the test of significance, confidence intervals, p-value, conclusion);
    Example 2, travel time between treatment and control (two-sample t-test,
    equal variances); Example 3, the causal effect of treatment on school
    enrolment.
-   **Extra materials for self-study**: the four steps of a t-test, from
    hypothesis formulation to conclusion, with examples.
-   **t-scores**: critical values of the t-distribution for 1 to 150 degrees of
    freedom.
-   Homework on two published field experiments and the key concepts
    checklist.

## Data used

-   `sleep` (Student's sleep data) from base R, for Example 1.
-   A one-variable example dataset from the data-to-viz project, downloaded at
    render time.
-   Simulated populations and samples for the travel-time and enrolment
    examples.
